U.S. electricity prices, bills and affordability

U.S. electricity prices for residential customers have been rising somewhat faster than inflation — making them a flashpoint for concerns about the cost of living and triggering a contentious debate about who is to blame. 

Residential electricity prices have increased at an average annual rate of roughly 5% compared with growth in all prices of just under 4% since 2019, according to estimates prepared by U.S. Energy Information Administration.  

Electricity prices have been rising faster than for other goods and services after a decade in which they were generally flat or falling in real terms, heightening the shock for users. 

Moreover, increases have been uneven, with much faster rises in the Northeast and states on the Pacific Coast than in the Midwest and the South.  

Price rises are therefore roiling politics in a broad swathe of states from Maine to Virginia in the East as well as California, Oregon and Hawaii in the West. 

Many of these states have ambitious targets for reducing emissions from generation and have also experienced the rapid deployment of data centres. 

Rising prices have therefore sparked an acrimonious debate about whether environmental policies or data centres are to blame ...

#Libya' *NOC Statement Regarding the Closure of the Zawiya Oil Complex by Protesters

This Monday morning, a group of personnel from the Petroleum Facilities Guard (PFG) blocked the gates of the Zawiya Oil Refining Company (Zawiya Refinery) and the Brega Petroleum Marketing Company. This action prevented employees and technicians from entering, blocked the handover of night shifts responsible for operational activities, and stopped students from the Zawiya Oil Training Institute from attending classes. Although the gate to the Brega Petroleum Marketing Company was subsequently partially reopened, the main gate to the Zawiya Refinery remains closed. This situation fails to meet the safety and occupational health standards required within the oil sector for the optimal resumption of operations.

These developments coincide with the ongoing closure of Valve No. 7 in the Hamada area—located on the Sharara crude oil pipeline—by PFG personnel from the southwest region and an armed group. This has halted the flow of crude oil from the Sharara field (operated by Akakus Oil Operations) to the Zawiya terminal, resulting in a daily loss of approximately 130,000 barrels—a figure expected to rise if the closure persists.

The National Oil Corporation (NOC) emphasizes that this closure exposes all operational activities at the oil complex to unpredictable technical, operational, and security risks. It violates public safety standards, threatening severe damage to vital facilities and equipment, and jeopardizing refining operations and oil supplies.  The Corporation warns that the continuation of this obstruction will result in the complete paralysis of operational activities within the complex. This will have a direct and immediate impact on fuel supplies and state revenues, while also disrupting the import and distribution of petroleum products to the domestic market—thereby driving up supply costs and compounding the daily hardships faced by citizens.

The National Oil Corporation calls upon those responsible for the blockade to exercise reason and wisdom, prioritize the national interest, immediately lift the blockade, and allow technical, operational, and administrative staff to carry out their duties. Furthermore, it urges the relevant authorities and security agencies to fulfill their national and legal responsibilities regarding the protection of oil facilities and the safety of personnel, ensuring these sites remain insulated from political disputes or factional demands.

The Corporation reiterates that oil and its vital infrastructure belong to all the Libyan people and that maintaining their continuous operation safeguards national assets and national security. It further clarifies that, in order to uphold its contractual obligations, the Board of Directors is currently preparing to declare *force majeure* within the coming hours if the valve is not reopened; this step is necessary to protect the assets of the Corporation and its partners and to avoid incurring heavy financial penalties for the Libyan state.

#Commodities
#Crudeoil trades lower for a sixth consecutive day as supply and diplomatic developments continue to erode the geopolitical risk premium. Saudi Arabia said it would soon restore exports through its East-West pipeline, while the US and Iran held a “very productive” meeting aimed at ending the war. With flows through the Strait already increasing and the Saudi pipeline restarting, Iran’s leverage appears to be weakening, helping push prices lower. Gasoil, the diesel and jet fuel feedstock, meanwhile holds near USD 200 per barrel, after Trump said he endorsed the idea of a diesel export ban, while highlighting that the main stress remains in refined products amid reduced capacity. Ahead of the weekly EIA report, API reported a 1.8-million-barrel rise in crude stocks, while gasoline and distillate inventories declined.
HG #Copper futures rose to a fresh record on Tuesday, briefly topping USD 6.90 per pound in New York before retreating to USD 6.82 this morning. While the US interest-rate outlook may provide a headwind, copper remains supported by strong underlying supply-and-demand fundamentals, including signs of pre-holiday tightening in China. According to Shanghai Metals Market, some imported copper has arrived, but much of it has gone directly to fabricators rather than warehouses, keeping spot supplies constrained.
#Gold continues to trade within its established narrow USD 4,300–4,400 range, with Fed comments and their impact on US rates, bond yields and the dollar, together with oil-price movements, providing the main direction for short-term traders. ETF holdings dipped slightly on Tuesday but have still seen inflows of around 48 tonnes this month, while China’s purchases through August topped 1,000 tonnes, already surpassing the whole of 2025.

Gasoil futures, the main feedstock to distillate products from diesel and jet fuel to heating oil and fuel oil, jumps 5.3% after Trump said he backs banning exports of diesel as soaring fuel prices squeeze American farmers and truckers and threaten to fuel further inflation ahead of November’s midterm elections. Brent now trades at a USD +103/b premium above gasoil  Chart source: Bloomberg
